- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment phases.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment; model fails to recognize bearish momentum.
- Lag in correction: model often delays downward adjustments after negative sentiment spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects upward after strong bullish sentiment, then underreacts to subsequent pullbacks.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; should align with 14-day sentiment trends for better calibration.
- High sentiment volatility → model overfits to recent highs; reduce forecast amplitude when sentiment swings sharply.
- Negative sentiment > -0.30 → model underestimates true price; apply +0.5 to forecast if sentiment < -0.30.
- Positive sentiment > 0.30 → model overestimates; apply -0.5 to forecast if sentiment > 0.30.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative after a peak, reduce forecast by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
